system_description.narrative_title: Far‑right surge in Germany and Europe destabilises centrist politics
system_description.narrative_summary: A wave of far‑right electoral gains — epitomised by the AfD’s victory in Saxony‑Anhalt — is precipitating crises for centre‑right governments (notably Friedrich Merz’s CDU), intensifying migration‑related protests and cross‑border political anxiety (France, UK, Sweden). The event is creating reinforcing feedbacks between electoral shifts, policy uncertainty, public unrest and institutional strain that could reshape coalition arithmetic, migration policy and European political norms.
system_description.scope: Electoral dynamics and party competition across Germany and neighbouring EU states; incumbent governments and coalition formation; public attitudes and protests over migration; law‑enforcement and institutional responses; media and cross‑border political signalling within Europe.
system_description.super_system: The stability of European democratic governance and its interaction with global geopolitical and economic trends (migration flows, economic stress, transatlantic norms).
adjacent_subsystems: Migration and border management (flows, asylum policy, enforcement)
EU institutions and cross‑border diplomacy (intergovernmental responses, sanctions on norms)
National security and law enforcement (public order, policing of protests)
Financial and market confidence (investor reaction to political risk)
evidence_headlines: Far-right AfD wins historic victory in German state election
Far-right AfD landslide in German state piles pressure on federal government
After Far-Right Election Breakthrough, Germany’s Merz Faces Painful Dilemma

France worried by victory of far-right's AfD in German state election
UK police face questions over anti-migrant protests by masked demonstrators

variables.name: Far‑right electoral support
variables.description: The proportion of the electorate expressing sustained voting support for radical right parties and candidates.

variables.name: Party‑system fragmentation
variables.description: The degree to which electoral support is distributed across multiple parties rather than concentrated in a few major parties.

variables.name: Coalition stability
variables.description: The likelihood that incumbent governing coalitions remain intact and can reliably pass legislation over time.

variables.name: Policy uncertainty
variables.description: The level of ambiguity and unpredictability about future public policy directions as perceived by political actors and stakeholders.

variables.name: Protest activity intensity
variables.description: The rate and scale of public demonstrations, rallies and street actions related to contentious political issues.

variables.name: Migration flow volume
variables.description: The net rate of cross‑border population movements into the polity over a given period.

variables.name: Public attitude toward migration
variables.description: Aggregate public sentiment ranging from supportive to oppositional regarding immigration and asylum policies.

variables.name: Institutional capacity for public order
variables.description: The ability of administrative and enforcement systems to manage public order, security incidents and large public events effectively.

variables.name: Media polarization
variables.description: The extent to which media outlets and information channels present highly divergent, partisan narratives on political issues.

variables.name: Public trust in political institutions
variables.description: The average level of citizen confidence in the legitimacy and competence of governing institutions and elected officials.

variables.name: Economic stress level
variables.description: The degree of macroeconomic and household financial pressure, including inflation, unemployment and cost‑of‑living strains.

variables.name: Electoral volatility
variables.description: The rate at which voters switch party preferences between electoral cycles, measured as aggregate vote share shifts.

variables.name: Pressure on rule‑of‑law institutions
variables.description: The degree of stress placed on judicial, oversight and legal institutions from politicized cases, legal challenges and institutional capture risks.

variables.name: Cross‑border political signalling
variables.description: The intensity and frequency of political messages, endorsements or rhetoric transmitted across borders that influence domestic political debates.

variables.name: Law‑enforcement legitimacy
variables.description: Public perception of the fairness, impartiality and normative legitimacy of policing and security forces.

variables.name: Social cohesion
variables.description: The strength of social ties, cross‑group trust and willingness to adhere to shared democratic norms among the population.

catalysts.title: Saxony-Anhalt government formation and coalition talks
catalysts.description: Post-election negotiations in Saxony-Anhalt will determine whether AfD gains governing influence or remains excluded, shaping regional power dynamics.
catalysts.rationale: AfD landslide in German state election; 'small German leftist party emerges as potential far-right kingmaker'; 'What next for AfD...'; 'What would AfD do in first 100 days?'

catalysts.title: CDU federal crisis and pressure on Merz
catalysts.description: Internal CDU turmoil and pressure on Chancellor Merz could trigger leadership battles or policy paralysis at the federal level.
catalysts.rationale: 'Germany’s Merz is running out of time'; 'Merz in shock'; 'Merz on the ropes after far right delivers devastating blow'; 'CDU in crisis after far-right victory'

catalysts.title: Upcoming regional/state elections in Germany
catalysts.description: A sequence of regional polls following Saxony-Anhalt could either consolidate or reverse the AfD surge, affecting national momentum.
catalysts.rationale: 'German state heads to regional polls in far-right cliffhanger'; multiple headlines on AfD surging to first place

catalysts.title: Sweden general election (looming)
catalysts.description: A tight Swedish election will test migration politics and the right/centre balance, potentially shifting regional narratives.
catalysts.rationale: 'Sweden election race tightens as Liberals make parliament threshold'; 'As election looms, Sweden's government is paying immigrants to leave'

catalysts.title: Anti‑migrant protests and local unrest in the UK
catalysts.description: Anti‑migrant demonstrations (e.g., Portsmouth) may escalate, testing police responses and local political messaging ahead of broader debates.
catalysts.rationale: 'UK minister condemns anti-migrant protests in Portsmouth'; 'Port demonstrations prompt questions for authorities'; 'Police face questions over anti-migrant protests by masked protesters'

catalysts.title: Negotiations for migrant return/deportation deals by EU states
catalysts.description: Five European nations seeking deals to send migrants out of the EU will alter migration management and political signalling across Europe.
catalysts.rationale: 'Five European nations seek deals to send migrants out of the EU'; complements Sweden paying immigrants to leave

catalysts.title: Cross‑border political signalling after AfD breakthrough
catalysts.description: The AfD's success will be used rhetorically across Europe, encouraging like‑minded movements and shifting media narratives.
catalysts.rationale: 'A German election result heard around the world'; 'The AfD Rises on the German Right'; numerous headlines on AfD surge and Europe worried by victory'

catalysts.title: Trial of suspected migrant smugglers in Paris
catalysts.description: The high‑profile trial over a mass drowning case will shape public debate on migration enforcement and culpability of smuggling networks.
catalysts.rationale: 'Suspected migrant smugglers go on trial in Paris over mass drowning in Channel'
